issue_context.title: AEMET OpenData provide a string for its state, while the device class is 'timestamp'
issue_context.body:
### The problem

After upgrading to 2021.12, home-assistant log request to create a bug report here.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2021.12.*

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

aemet

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
2021-12-21 18:59:03 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.sensor] sensor.aemet_town_timestamp is providing a string for its state, while the device class is 'timestamp', this is not valid and will be unsupported from Home Assistant 2022.2. Please create a bug report at https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3A%22integration%3A+aemet%22

2021-12-21 18:59:03 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.sensor] sensor.aemet_daily_forecast_time is providing a string for its state, while the device class is 'timestamp', this is not valid and will be unsupported from Home Assistant 2022.2. Please create a bug report at https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3A%22integration%3A+aemet%22

2021-12-21 18:59:03 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.sensor] sensor.aemet_hourly_forecast_time is providing a string for its state, while the device class is 'timestamp', this is not valid and will be unsupported from Home Assistant 2022.2. Please create a bug report at https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3A%22integration%3A+aemet%22
2
```


### Additional information

_No response_

Hey there @noltari, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`aemet`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L34) for? Thanks!

review_comments: If nothing else depends on this and `elaborated` is already timezone aware, we could just return that without converting to UTC time. The base sensor class will convert to UTC time for us.
I think it's better to convert to force the UTC conversion to keep consistency with the rest of the code (station_timestamp, daily/hourly ATTR_FORECAST_TIME).

Would be nice to move this case to a lambda function in the entity description.

Example:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/08a3140e6cbffc5677971f98191e24eea7085236/homeassistant/components/airly/sensor.py#L100
